family: ATI R300 and R350 (FireGL X1, FireGL X2; SGI Onyx4)

bases.label: board record +656
bases.why: the kernel object's register accessors load the register aperture base from board record +656 and add the byte offset they are given

bases.label: device record +1000
bases.why: firegl_addmap stores the mapped register aperture at device record +1000; the interrupt, vsync and reset paths load it from there

bases.label: driver record +48
bases.why: the X module's register accessors load the mapped register aperture from the driver record at +48 (reached through the screen's private pointer at +248)

bases.label: register base argument
bases.why: both PLL helpers index off their first argument, the mapped register base

scope.reason: MIPS CPU exception vectors, TLB refill and maintenance, user-fault and FPU emulation: generic kernel code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use
CPU cache and branch-predictor maintenance primitives: generic kernel code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use
C library, memory copy, user-access and checksum routines: generic kernel code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use
Kernel atomics, locks, interrupt-priority-level helpers, timers, clocks and scheduler hooks: generic kernel code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use
Hardware performance counters (R1x000, memory directory, I/O): CPU and platform measurement, no graphics register, token or ioctl use
Platform error logging, memory and directory error handling, poison and page-protection bookkeeping, NMI and crash-dump support: platform code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use
Router, NUMAlink and node-board topology discovery, inventory and diagnostics: platform code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use
Flash PROM, CFI flash, PROM log and NVRAM dictionary access: firmware storage code with no graphics register, token or ioctl use

Software OpenGL in the ATI driver: display-list recording and playback, no-op extension placeholders, pixel span, image-format conversion and texel extraction run on the host CPU and touch no board register, token or ioctl

OpenGL API entry points and immediate-mode dispatch wrappers (glFoo, __glim_Foo for the variants other than R300): thin argument-forwarding layer with no chip state of its own; the R300-named variants and the R100- and R200-named variants stay in scope

Host-CPU software rendering and geometry pipeline (clipping, transform, vertex assembly and copy, span stores, non-native copies, convolution, feedback, evaluators): no chip register or command-packet emission; a function is excluded only by these name families

Bridge ASIC register accessors (one get or set routine per register field): they belong to the bridge chip, not to the R300 or R350 board behind it, and no board register, token or ioctl is reached here; the attach, mapping, interrupt and DMA routines stay in scope

Generic X server core (protocol dispatch, fonts, Xkb, XDMCP, authorisation, mi and fb rendering, input, extensions): no graphics register, token or ioctl use; the PCI, int10, DRI and video-memory routines stay in scope
Generic GLX protocol decoding and byte-swapping in the X server: dispatch and request-size tables with no board-specific state; no graphics register, token or ioctl use
Software OpenGL core in the X server (indirect rendering): immediate-mode, display-list, span and pixel code runs on the host CPU; no graphics register, token or ioctl use
IRIS GL compatibility layer over OpenGL: legacy API translation in user space with no board-specific state; no graphics register, token or ioctl use
OpenGL client entry points and GLX request marshalling: thin dispatch and protocol encoding; the board attach, pipe and drawable routines stay in scope

Public x86 emulator core used to run the option ROM (opcode handlers, ALU primitives, operand decoding): generic instruction interpretation, the same code as the public X server module; the I/O, memory and interrupt hooks and the BIOS set-up stay in scope
Public x86 emulator operand decoding: generic instruction interpretation; the execute and halt entry points stay in scope
Generic C library random-number and GLU helpers linked into the diagnostic: no graphics register, token or ioctl use

Motif/ViewKit user-interface classes and callbacks of the combine tool, plus its symbol-database file code: no graphics register, token or ioctl use; the format-file, query and command-line routines stay in scope
